# Claims register

Every important architectural claim with its truth class.

- **A**: publicly documented mechanism (needs a source link or a `repo@commit:path#Lx-Ly` citation)
- **B**: common production design
- **C**: reference-architecture choice
- **D**: proprietary or unknown (never stated as fact)

Merged: notes 01, 01b, 02 to 07 and 09, plus corrections from 08-verification. Source column uses global IDs from `sources.md`; code citations are copied as written. The Class column keeps the note's own qualifier in brackets (for example "A (derived: ...)"). The "Used in" column lists the manuscript sections that use the claim. The notes' claims tables carry no requirement IDs, so that column shows "-" except where noted. Claims in note 07 had no "date checked" column; its header states 2026-10-09 for every row.

## Phase 3 verification (2026-10-09)

Method: the 1,588 class A rows with a non-empty "Used in" were checked against the cited source, or against the pinned repo for code citations, by six verifier agents (reports `research/verification/phase3-<range>.md`); the 41 rows first marked unverifiable were re-read in full text (`phase3-unverifiable.md`, whose verdict overrides the first pass). Code citations were re-pinned to vllm@v0.31.0 and sglang@v0.5.21. Fixes are logged in `phase3-fixes-00-08.md`, `phase3-fixes-09-16.md` and `phase3-fixes-17-25.md`. Final verdicts: 1538 confirmed, 32 corrected, 8 citation moved, 3 reclassified B|C, 5 register only, 2 unverifiable (total 1588). "Register only" means the manuscript was right and the register row was stale or already worded correctly. Each ID appears once.

## Part 20 mapping: rows added for claims the chapter makes

Rows added while mapping `manuscript/part-20-other-branches.md`. The Source column is exactly as cited in the chapter; "none cited in chapter" means the sentence carries no citation (a bracket such as (RA-14) or (part 14.6) names the reference-architecture row or cross-reference the sentence relies on, and a `hypothetical.*` path names the constants group that holds the value; "derived" means arithmetic from cited or hypothetical values). Class follows the chapter wording: results of the estimates and worked examples are class C because their inputs are hypothetical; definitions and mechanisms stated as fact are class A; "a common" design statements are class B; what is not public is class D. New rows are CL-2766 to CL-2911.

## Part 24 mapping: rows added for claims the chapter makes

Rows added while mapping `manuscript/part-24-build-a-miniature.md`. The Source column is exactly as cited in the chapter; "none cited in chapter" means the sentence carries no citation (a bracket such as (RA-40) or (part 9.3) names the reference-architecture row or cross-reference the sentence relies on). The chapter labels its code as illustrative: it runs a fake model, a toy tokenizer and a virtual clock. So every statement about the miniature itself (its components, its run trace, its numbers, its variants) has the class "illustrative (Part 24 sim)", not class A. Class A is kept for public mechanisms stated as fact (asyncio, vLLM, Sarathi-Serve, llm-d, RRF); class B for statements of a common stack; class C for statements about the reference system (they carry an RA-nn). The chapter has no class D statement. New rows are CL-3184 to CL-3309.

### Terminology

- Part 09 §9.1 to §9.3 call the unit the inference gateway picks an "endpoint" (one per DEP16 rank, RA-71); Parts 00, 01, 02, 05 and 08 call the same pick a "GPU replica" or "model server replica", and the glossary defines endpoint as the address of a model server. In Part 09 an endpoint is a rank, not a model server. SYNONYM/scope problem: either add "one rank" to the glossary entry for endpoint or say once that a replica holds 16 endpoints.
- "tier" has four meanings in Part 09: "tier two" of the Agent Router (model router), the "three tiers" of EPP dispatch (priority, fairness, ordering), "user tier" (plan), and the KV memory tiers G1 to G3. The glossary lists only band for priority; use "stage" for the dispatch order.
- §9.4 writes "queue length" once in the inputs table; the glossary term is queue depth.
- "the gateway" alone (§9.1 `failureMode`, §9.4 "waits at the gateway", §9.6 "the gateway layer") can mean the API gateway, the inference gateway or Envoy; the glossary forbids "router (alone)" for inference gateway but not "gateway (alone)".
- "wait limit" (§9.4, §9.6) is the 60 s TTL; Part 02 says "waits at most 60 s" and the header says `rejected-ttl-expired`. One term is enough: wait limit.
- "hit share" (§9.2 tables), "hit rate" (§9.2 signals table) and "prefix-hit share" name the same ratio at two scopes (tokens versus requests); pick one.
